descriptions.browse_file: Use when you need the outline of ONE file you can already name: its complete symbol table, with filtering, sorting and optional imports and stats. The outline is source-derived, so it stands in for opening the file to check symbol names, signatures or line numbers.
descriptions.callers: Use when you need the confirmed call sites of one named symbol: a resolved call-graph query rather than a text scan, with callers grouped by enclosing function and each call-site line and count, and dynamic-dispatch or unresolved sites listed separately.
descriptions.code_insight: Use when you need a report about the codebase as a whole rather than one symbol: high-level overview, detailed analysis, code statistics, structure or git analysis, selected by mode (overview, detailed, statistics, unified, structure, git_analyze, git_hotspots).
descriptions.context: Use when you need to carry code context across agent sessions: 'save' captures a compact 2-5KB manifest of symbol references, and 'load' hydrates it back into full context with source code and call graphs, so the next session does not repeat the exploration.
descriptions.debug_info: Use when you need to troubleshoot the index itself: symbol distribution, type breakdown, reference statistics and file-level detail. Reach for it when index_stats reports problems or when relationship queries come back empty.
descriptions.find_files: Use when you need to locate files by PATH rather than by content - the 'find' or 'fd' job, answered from an in-memory index, with fuzzy matching, glob patterns and filters.
descriptions.get_context: Use when you need detailed context for code objects you can already identify: signature, file path, line numbers, callers and callees, references, a source excerpt and snippets, intended to replace opening the source file.
descriptions.git_analysis: Use when you need to judge the quality of your git changes before committing: new or modified code compared against the existing codebase for duplicate code, naming inconsistencies and function complexity, over the 'staged', 'wip', 'commit' or 'range' scope.
descriptions.index_stats: Use when you need to know whether the index is ready and healthy: indexing progress, component health, memory usage and file-watcher status - the tool for diagnosing 'index not ready' or searches that return empty.
descriptions.info: Use when you need help on the tools themselves: an overview of what this server offers, detailed help and examples for one named tool, or the server version.
descriptions.inspect_symbol: Use when you need everything known about ONE symbol, given its name or object ID: signature, doc, complexity, callers, callees, type hierarchy, scope chain, flags and a bounded source excerpt.
descriptions.list_symbols: Use when you need to enumerate and filter symbols across the index - the 'ls' for code - by kind, file, complexity, parameter count and exported status, to discover what exists without searching for it.
descriptions.search: Use when you need to find code by its text or meaning across the corpus, in place of grep, rg or find. Results are grouped per file with per-hit line numbers, and symbol hits carry an id that feeds get_context.
descriptions.semantic_annotations: Use when you need symbols by semantic LABEL or category rather than by text: direct @lci: annotations, external annotation manifests, and labels propagated through call graphs.
descriptions.side_effects: Use when you need to know whether a function is pure: writes to parameters, globals and closures, I/O operations and exception handling, optionally followed transitively through the call graph.
